items.title: pyminleon
items.text:
pyminleon is an asyncio Python library that controls the built-in effects of Minleon NDB-Pro LED controllers over the HTTP endpoints the controller's own web UI uses. Zero runtime dependencies (stdlib only), Python 3.12+.

It does not send pixel data. For that, use a DDP sender such as aioddp. While DDP data flows it overrides the built-in effect; about 20 s after DDP stops the controller falls back to it.

Guide Safety What the library will and will not send to a controller. Reference API reference NDBController, identify and the error types — generated from docstrings.

items.title: Installation
items.text: pip install pyminleon

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
import asyncio

from pyminleon import NDBController, identify


async def main() -> None:
    host = "10.0.40.20"  # placeholder
    if await identify(host) is None:
        raise SystemExit("not a supported Minleon controller")

    ndb = NDBController(host)
    state = await ndb.state()  # NDBState(effect="Glow", intensity=100, effects=("Off", ..., "Worms"))
    await ndb.set_effect("Color Wave")
    await ndb.set_intensity(60)
    await ndb.recall_preset(3)  # slots 0-9 are "Show 1", 10-19 "Show 2"
    layout = await ndb.config()  # raw JSON from GET /api/config (DDP-spec layout document)
    print(state, layout["config"]["ports"][0], (await ndb.status())["status"]["mod"])


asyncio.run(main())

items.title: API overview
items.text:
• NDBController(host, *, port=80, timeout=3.0)
    • await state() -> NDBState selected effect, intensity, and every effect the controller offers
    • await presets() -> tuple[NDBPreset, ...] stored show slots
    • await set_effect(name), await set_intensity(percent), await recall_preset(slot)
    • await config() -> dict[str, Any], await status() -> dict[str, Any] raw /api/config and /api/status documents
  • await identify(host, *, port=80, timeout=3.0) -> str | None the model id (e.g. "NDBPRO") if the host reports a model in SUPPORTED_MODELS; None if it answers but is not a supported Minleon, or does not answer in time
  • Errors: MinleonError > ConfigError (bad host, port, timeout, or argument), ControllerError (unreachable, timed out, non-200, or an unreadable page or document)

The API reference documents every public name.

items.title: pyminleon.ndb
items.text:
Control of the Minleon NDB-Pro over the HTTP endpoints its own web UI uses.

It selects the controller's built-in effects, sets their intensity, and recalls stored show presets; it never writes the controller's saved settings (no saveon, no preset Set, no ?s=N). The controller exposes its effect state only as HTML, so state and presets read the UI pages with strict regexes and raise ControllerError when the markup is not what firmware 2.0 serves. config and status return the raw JSON documents from /api/config and /api/status. Stdlib only.

DDP pixel data overrides the built-in effect while it flows; about 20 s after DDP stops the controller falls back to it.

items.title: SUPPORTED_MODELS
items.text: Model ids (the mod field of /api/status) that pyminleon supports.

items.title: NDBController Objects
items.text:
class NDBController()

Selects and reads the built-in effects of a Minleon NDB-Pro over plain HTTP.

Every call is one or two short HTTP/1.0 requests bounded by timeout each. ControllerError means the controller could not be reached, timed out, answered with a status other than 200, or answered with a page or document pyminleon cannot read.

Set the built-in effect intensity, 0 to 100 percent.

items.title: recall_preset
items.text:
async def recall_preset(slot: int) -> None

Recall stored show slot slot (0-9 are "Show 1", 10-19 "Show 2"). Never saves.

items.title: identify
items.text:
async def identify(host: str,
                   *,
                   port: int = 80,
                   timeout: float = 3.0) -> str | None

The supported model id (e.g. "NDBPRO") at host, or None.

None means the host did not answer in time, did not answer GET /api/status with a JSON status, or reports a model not in SUPPORTED_MODELS. ConfigError for a bad host, port, or timeout.

items.title: pyminleon._http
items.text:
A minimal asyncio HTTP/1.0 client for talking to Minleon controllers on the LAN. Private; stdlib only.

One asyncio.timeout bounds connect, request, head, and body together, so a server dripping one byte at a time cannot stall a caller. Head and body are size-capped, redirects are never followed, and the host is validated so it can never steer the path, port, or scheme.

items.title: Response Objects
items.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Response()

Status code (None if unparsable) and body; the body is read only for a 200 (None otherwise).

items.title: url_host
items.text:
def url_host(host: str) -> str

host as it goes in a URL: a hostname or IPv4 address as is, an IPv6 literal bracketed.

items.title: url
items.text:
def url(host: str, port: int, path: str) -> str

http://HOST:PORT/PATH; host must be a hostname, IPv4 address, or IPv6 literal (brackets optional).

items.title: request
items.text:
async def request(host: str,
                  port: int,
                  path: str,
                  *,
                  timeout: float,
                  method: str = "GET",
                  body: bytes | None = None) -> Response

One HTTP/1.0 exchange under one deadline. Redirects are never followed.

Raises ConfigError for a bad host or path, ControllerError for a body over MAX_BODY, and one of TRANSPORT_ERRORS when the exchange fails or the deadline passes.

items.title: Safety
items.text:
pyminleon talks to a controller through its own web UI endpoints, so it is deliberately narrow about what it sends.

  • Nothing is ever written to the controller's saved settings. The library never requests /pshows.html?s=N (which overwrites a preset slot) and never sends saveon. The only requests it makes are POST /api/control, GET /pshows.html?r=N (recall), and read-only pages (/pfx2.html, /pcolors.html, /pshows.html, /api/config, /api/status).
  • Strict parsing. state() and presets() parse the web UI's HTML with strict patterns written against firmware 2.0 and raise ControllerError on anything else rather than guessing.
  • Bounded I/O. HTTP responses are size-capped (64 KiB), redirects are never followed, and each call is bounded by timeout.
  • Validated hosts. Hosts are validated (hostname, IPv4, or IPv6 literal only) so a value can never steer the path, port, or scheme.
